clue.text: Living in tower

definitions.meaning: your ... is your board and lodging, what you live on
a castle's ... is its central fortified tower

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: earning one's keep means one's livelihood, and the keep is a castle's main stronghold.

clue.text: Near water, he launched vessels

indicators.note: launched suggests letters sent flying off into a new order, an anagram signal here

explanation.surface: A man by the waterside sends boats off down the slipway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launched' reads as boats leaving the slip, but it tells you to rearrange NEAR WATER HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots and dishes of fired clay are vessels in the sense of containers, so earthenware is a collective for them.

clue.text: Man on train raised head, absorbed by mobile phone

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pager is a portable messaging device, loosely a mobile phone

indicators.note: in a down clue a raised word is read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A rail traveller looks up from his phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works because this is a down clue, so the headland is read upwards; a pager counts as a mobile phone only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling on a train who is not crew is a passenger, a fare-paying traveller.

clue.text: In last resting place, honour poet and soldier

indicators.note: In places the honour and the poet within the resting place

parts.note: a bier is the stand a coffin rests on before burial
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet and a soldier are honoured at the graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resting place' is the stand a coffin lies on, not the grave, and the honour is the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the British artillery, so a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Where customs patrol, say, for pirate?

indicators.note: say signals a word as spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: customs officers watch a national border

explanation.surface: A question about where customs men keep watch for smugglers.
explanation.walkthrough: A pirate who boards a ship is a boarder; the question mark flags that slightly playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates storm a vessel by climbing aboard it, so one of them is a boarder in a punning sense.

clue.text: Good news as some countries become free

indicators.note: letters that become free are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Independence for several nations is welcome tidings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become free' looks like the story of the countries, but it tells you to rearrange AS SOME COUNTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything delightful to hear, which is exactly what good news is.

clue.text: Commonwealth, in general, holds a E parliament

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: The Commonwealth generally contains a European parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across commonwe-ALTH IN G-eneral. The 'a E' before 'parliament' looks like an OCR fragment, probably of 'European'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Althing is Iceland's national legislature, one of the oldest parliaments in the world.

clue.text: Looked smug as sergeant-major marched off, annoyed

indicators.note: marched off says that piece leaves, taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to smirk is to smile in a smug way

explanation.surface: A soldier grins smugly as the sergeant-major stomps away irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Irked is a direct synonym of annoyed, both meaning irritated.

clue.text: In downfall, new quarrel

indicators.note: In puts the new piece inside the downfall

parts.note: ruin is a downfall, a collapse

explanation.surface: A fresh row breaks out as someone falls from grace.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an informal word for an argument or clash, so a quarrel.

clue.text: Matching glasses one used to receive long ago

definitions.meaning: a set of crystal drinking glasses that match

definitions.text: one used to receive long ago
definitions.meaning: an early radio receiver using a crystal detector

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a matched group of glassware and the simple wireless sets of the 1920s.

clue.text: It's related Edward VIII was, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Edward VIII was a king, briefly, since he abdicated within a year

explanation.surface: A remark about the short reign of the abdicating monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' works twice in the surface: Edward VIII reigned for under a year, and A KING loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means of the same kin or family, hence related.

clue.text: Plateau where you may find your bearings

definitions.meaning: in geology a ... is a vast ancient rock platform, like the Canadian ...

definitions.text: where you may find your bearings
definitions.meaning: heraldic bearings, the charges of a coat of arms

explanation.definitionFit: Geology names broad stable rock plateaus this way, and heraldry puts armorial bearings on one.

clue.text: Indian administrator to study mansion used for set

parts.note: Robert Clive governed Bengal for the East India Company
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: A colonial official goes to study at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliveden is a Buckinghamshire mansion that gave its name to the Cliveden Set, a political circle of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: The house where the Astors hosted the influential 1930s circle known after it as the Cliveden Set.

clue.text: Aircraft's emergency propeller?

parts.note: a propeller usually drives the plane, but here it is what propels the pilot out in a crisis

explanation.surface: A question about a backup propeller for a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A military jet's escape seat fires the pilot clear in an emergency, propelling a person rather than the craft.

clue.text: He joined the bar

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'He joined the bar' (4) for SNUG: no wordplay or definition reading gives SNUG from these words, and a search found no fuller text; the clue looks cut short.

clue.text: A couple of beers? That'll spice up the Chinese meal

definitions.text: That'll spice up the Chinese meal

parts.note: root beer is a fizzy drink flavoured with roots
ginger beer is a fizzy ginger drink

explanation.surface: Ordering two beers to go with a Chinese takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The two beers are root beer and ginger beer, each giving its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh ginger rhizome is a staple flavouring that adds heat to Chinese dishes.

clue.text: Tense situation, having to catch vicious dog

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them
a dog that bites is a biter

explanation.surface: A nervy moment trying to grab a savage dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliffhanger that makes people chew their fingernails is a nail-biter, a tense situation.

clue.text: Untouchable carcass not to be moved

indicators.note: letters to be moved are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dead body must be left exactly where it lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be moved' says CARCASS NOT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanct means too sacred to be violated, hence untouchable.

clue.text: Superficial harm from excessive bathing

parts.note: bathing here is sunbathing, and the superficial harm is to the skin's surface

explanation.surface: Overdoing a swim or a bath does you surface damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Too long sunbathing reddens and damages the skin's outer layer, an injury on the surface.

clue.text: Landing place below hill in Riviera resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the landing place under the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a quay is a wharf where boats land

explanation.surface: A harbour under a hill in a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay is a Devon seaside town on the stretch of coast nicknamed the English Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquay is the main town of the English Riviera in Devon, so a resort on a Riviera.

clue.text: Tiny piece of moon? Thanks

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Grateful for a fragment of the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is the smallest Greek letter, used to mean a tiny amount.

clue.text: I believe what writer needs is to be immersed in the spirit

indicators.note: being immersed in something means going inside it

parts.note: meths is methylated spirit
a writer needs ink

explanation.surface: An author needs to soak himself in alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the spirit' is methylated spirit, called meths in Britain; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Methinks is the archaic way of saying it seems to me, so I believe.

clue.text: Bride's announcement made catty remark

definitions.meaning: a cat mews, so a catty remark is a mew

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a bride's happy cry; as one it is the past of a cat's cry.

clue.text: Florence Dombey's admirer sounds horny

definitions.meaning: The bashful admirer of Florence in Dickens's Dombey and Son
a horn ..., so it gives a horn's sound

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens named Florence's lovesick suitor Toots, and the same word is what a horn does when blown.

clue.text: Boy has to dress right

parts.note: to robe is to dress

explanation.surface: A lad has to put on the proper clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert is a boy's name, an example of the class.

clue.text: Something woven from bark

definitions.meaning: the weft, the crosswise threads woven into cloth

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old weaving term for weft threads and the sound a dog makes.

clue.text: Where koala may be in trouble

definitions.meaning: koalas live in eucalyptus, gum trees
the idiom means in a difficult fix

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase places a koala in a eucalyptus; as an idiom it means stuck in difficulty.

clue.text: Graft finally established one's plant

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: one's read as one is, I'S
honesty is a garden plant with papery seed pods

explanation.surface: Someone's plant is at last rooted in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graft' looks like a horticultural term to go with 'plant'; it is the definition, meaning corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft in the sense of bribery and corrupt dealing is a form of dishonesty.

clue.text: Luxury in eastern half of Biscay resort

indicators.note: in an across clue the eastern half of a word is its right-hand, final half

parts.note: Biarritz is a French resort on the Bay of Biscay

explanation.surface: Luxury is found in the east side of a Biscay holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ritz hotels stand for luxury, as in 'putting on the Ritz'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz hotel name has become a byword for opulence, so it means luxury.
